lab_title: Structural Anatomy of the Human Heart and Blood Flow Through the Heart
top_level_objectives: Identify the four chambers of the heart.
Locate the four major heart valves and explain their role in preventing backflow.
Identify the major vessels entering and leaving the heart.
Trace the path of deoxygenated and oxygenated blood through pulmonary and systemic circulation.
Relate ventricular wall thickness to differences in pumping workload.

scenes.brief_purpose: Introduce the heart’s position, overall shape, and major external vessels as the starting framework for deeper study.
key_visuals: A 3D heart model in anatomical orientation within the thorax
Visible aorta, venae cavae, pulmonary trunk, pulmonary arteries, and pulmonary veins
Color cues distinguishing deoxygenated and oxygenated blood pathways
student_actions: Inspect the heart from anterior and superior views
Identify where major vessels enter and exit
Use labels to distinguish right and left sides in anatomical orientation

scenes.brief_purpose: Help students identify the right atrium, right ventricle, left atrium, and left ventricle and understand their basic receiving versus pumping roles.
key_visuals: Cutaway heart showing all four chambers
Color-highlighted right and left sides
Relative size and wall thickness differences between chambers
student_actions: Select each chamber by name
Match each chamber with whether it receives or pumps blood
Compare the left and right ventricles visually

scenes.brief_purpose: Introduce the tricuspid, pulmonary, mitral, and aortic valves as structures that enforce one-way blood movement.
key_visuals: Internal heart view with all four valves highlighted
Animated valve opening and closing
Simple arrows showing permitted flow direction and blocked backflow
student_actions: Locate each valve between the correct chambers or vessels
Match each valve to its position and blood pathway
Observe how valve motion changes during pumping and prevents reverse flow

scenes.scene_name: Pulmonary Circuit: Right Heart to Lungs
scenes.brief_purpose: Trace deoxygenated blood from the body through the right side of the heart to the lungs.
key_visuals: Animated flow entering via superior and inferior vena cava
Path through right atrium, tricuspid valve, right ventricle, pulmonary valve, and pulmonary arteries
Lung destination highlighted to show gas exchange target
student_actions: Follow the deoxygenated blood path step by step
Sequence the structures in correct order
Differentiate pulmonary arteries from systemic arteries by what kind of blood they carry

scenes.scene_name: Systemic Circuit: Left Heart to Body
scenes.brief_purpose: Trace oxygenated blood from the lungs through the left side of the heart and out to the body.
key_visuals: Animated flow returning by pulmonary veins
Path through left atrium, mitral valve, left ventricle, aortic valve, and aorta
Body circulation destination highlighted
student_actions: Follow the oxygenated blood path step by step
Sequence the structures in correct order
Contrast pulmonary veins with typical veins by what kind of blood they carry

scenes.scene_name: Why the Left Ventricle Is Thicker
scenes.brief_purpose: Connect structural differences in myocardium thickness to functional differences in circulation demands.
key_visuals: Cross-sectional comparison of right and left ventricular walls
Pressure or workload comparison graphic
Pulmonary loop versus systemic loop shown side by side
student_actions: Compare ventricular wall thickness visually
Explain why the left ventricle needs more force
Link chamber structure to the distance and resistance of each circuit

scenes.brief_purpose: Synthesize chamber, valve, vessel, and circulation knowledge into a complete pathway of blood through the heart.
key_visuals: Full heart model with removable labels or pathway markers
Mixed oxygenation color coding across the whole route
Optional cardiac cycle loop showing repeated circulation
student_actions: Build or recite the complete blood pathway in order
Place chambers, valves, and vessels into the correct sequence
Answer a final prompt about where backflow would occur if a valve failed
